question: How many jobs will the U.S. economy add in October 2026?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: 2026 initial NFP prints (Jan ~130k est., Feb ~-92k est., Mar 178k, Jun 57k, Jul 21k, Aug 162k, Sep 29k) mean ~70k, SD ~75k. Trend weakening: 3-mo avg 51k, Sep 29k vs ~84-90k consensus, Jul-Aug revised down 60k, labor-supply constraints. Offsets: claims ~197k near 57-yr lows, ADP Sep +90k, low prints often followed by rebounds. Polymarket bucket ladder (thin, $0.5-12k vol each; same BLS first-print contract) implies median ~60k with ~30% >=100k, ~3% in 0 to -25k; consistent with my median. Tails priced for a strike/weather/weak-economy negative print and an August-style rebound above 160k. No 2026 shutdown found disrupting the Nov 6 release.
calls.dossier:
- Resolves off BLS Employment Situation first print for Oct 2026 (Total nonfarm SA change, nearest thousand), scheduled Fri 2026-11-06 8:30 ET (BLS Sep release). Later revisions are not used.
- Event window: October 2026 reference month -> first print 2026-11-06; as of 2026-10-12 the reference month is ~37% elapsed and the reference week (week containing Oct 12) is now in progress.
- Sep 2026 first print +29k vs Dow Jones consensus ~84k (others ~89-90k); UE rate 4.2% (BLS/CNBC, 2026-10-02).
- Revisions: Jul revised from +21k to -10k, Aug from +162k to +133k; together -60k (BLS 2026-10-02).
- 3-month avg 51k/month (Indeed Hiring Lab, TD, 2026-10-02); breakeven usually cited at ~100-125k, possibly lower given reduced immigration and retirements.
- 2026 first or near-first prints: Jan ~130k (later revised to 160k), Feb negative (later -133k), Mar +178k, Jun +57k, Jul +21k, Aug +162k, Sep +29k. Searched for Apr/May first prints: not found (May later shown as 129k after revision). Spread of initial prints this year is roughly -100k to +180k; SD ~70-80k.
- ADP private payrolls Sep +90k vs ~68-70k expected; Aug revised to 36k (ADP 2026-09-30).
- Initial jobless claims 197k for week ending Oct 3, near 57-year lows for 4 straight weeks; 'low-hire, low-fire' (US News/Reuters 2026-10-08).
- Macro: the Fed has hiked in 2026; CPI around 3.7% expected; wage growth at a 5-year low of 3.0% y/y (TD).
- Sep sectors: healthcare +17k, construction +11k, manufacturing +9k, financial -7k, government down.
- Not found: an October consensus forecast, any 2026 government shutdown affecting the Nov 6 release, or a strike or hurricane affecting the October reference week.
- Status quo: continuation of the recent ~50k-trend pace with high month-to-month noise (first-print surprise vs consensus often +/-60-80k).

calls.reconciliation: The runs agreed closely once units are aligned. Runs 2 and 3 reported their percentiles in thousands (e.g. 55, 60), while the question's bounds (-39500..160500) and its 57,000 example show units are jobs; read in jobs, all three medians sit at 55-62k. The second dispute was each run's list of 2026 first prints (Run 1: Feb negative, Mar 178k; Run 3: 68, 71, 57...). It doesn't change the reference-class median (~60k) or the spread, so I left it unsettled. I ran no searches because no remaining factual dispute was decision-relevant. On judgment, I lean slightly below the Polymarket-implied ~60k because of the September miss and the downward revision trend, offset by low claims. I carried Run 1's reference class and dispersion forward with minor narrowing because the percentiles are conditional on landing inside the range.
